term: three years unless war sooner ended
age_rule: between eighteen and thirty-five at call
assignment: fill existing companies from same state to maximum; excess held as reserve
exemptions: legally exempt persons excluded; April 21 act follows
notes: Authority and eligibility, not a numbered quota or an observed intake. Volunteering into existing companies allowed before enrollment.
Do not backdate this act to April 16; five-day interval retained.

term: three years or during the war
assignment: chiefly infantry recommended; governor and federal mustering channels
exemptions: no universal exemption list supplied for volunteer call
notes: Lincoln letter dated July 1 promises quotas tomorrow; August regulations call it the July 2 call. Not 300000 available men on July 2.

term: President specifies period not exceeding nine months
age_rule: able-bodied male citizens between eighteen and forty-five
assignment: apportioned by representative population; militia organization as for volunteers
exemptions: enrollment rules authorized where state laws defective

assignment: acceptance authority additional to existing volunteer authority
notes: First month pay and 25 dollars bounty on company/regiment muster. Authority ceiling, not 100000 raised.
50 dollars bounty: half on joining regiment, half at expiration; do not create another national numbered call.

age_rule: see July 17 act and August 9 regulations
assignment: Secretary assigns state quotas; governors administer
notes: Separate from July volunteers. Failure to furnish July quota by August 15 invokes additional special draft; Aug 5 circular prints August 18 instead (OR32 pp.295-296). Preserve both versions.

term: nine months for August militia; no term conversion for July deficiency inferred
age_rule: able-bodied male citizens eighteen to forty-five
assignment: governors enroll and apportion; county commissioners determine exemptions; muster remains federal
exemptions: OR32 p.334 classes and state-law exemptions; substitute conditions pp.334-335
notes: Existing service struck off list; deadline language August 15 unless otherwise ordered; rendezvous within five days of drafting. 101 men per company and ten companies per regiment are prescribed organization, not actual unit strength.

term: three years unless war sooner ended
age_rule: between thirty-five and forty-five; continuing authority over those reaching eighteen
assignment: first fill same-state organizations existing April 16; surplus to later/new organizations
exemptions: legally exempt at call; October act replaces April exemptions
notes: Partial call must begin with lower ages; suspension permitted where execution impracticable. Not evidence all through forty-five were immediately called.
Classes conditional on actual occupation; slavery-policing provisions require separate sensitive-history review before any authored effect. No population resource authored.

age_rule: between eighteen and forty; Davis expressly limits current call to men under forty
notes: Distinguish law authorizing through forty-five from current executive enrollment limit. Randolph population estimates on p.132 are his estimates from 1850 census, not a measured field force.
